title: Three Areas in a Hexagon
statement: Point $P$ lies inside the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$. Triangles $PAB$, $PBC$ and $PCD$ have areas $7$, $10$ and $15$ respectively. What is the area of the hexagon?
hints: Each of the triangles $PAB$, $PBC$, $\dots$, $PFA$ has a side of the hexagon as its base, so its area is half the side length times the distance from $P$ to that side. Compare these distances for a pair of opposite sides, and for the three sides $AB$, $CD$ and $EF$.

Opposite sides of the hexagon are parallel, so the distances from $P$ to $BC$ and to $EF$ add up to the distance between those two lines. The lines $AB$, $CD$ and $EF$ form an equilateral triangle containing $P$, and the distances from a point inside an equilateral triangle to its three sides add up to its height.

Write $[XYZ]$ for the area of triangle $XYZ$ and $H$ for the area of the hexagon. These two facts give $[PBC] + [PEF] = \frac{1}{3}H$ and $[PAB] + [PCD] + [PEF] = \frac{1}{2}H$. Subtract one equation from the other.
solution:
Write $[XYZ]$ for the area of triangle $XYZ$. Let $s$ be the side of the hexagon and $a$ the distance from its centre $O$ to each side, so that the triangles $OAB, \dots, OFA$ give the hexagon area $H = 6 \cdot \frac{1}{2}sa = 3sa$. A triangle with apex $P$ and a side of the hexagon as base has area $\frac{1}{2}s$ times the distance from $P$ to that side.

As $BC$ and $EF$ are parallel and $2a$ apart, $[PBC] + [PEF] = sa = \frac{1}{3}H$. The lines $AB$, $CD$ and $EF$ form an equilateral triangle with incentre $O$ and inradius $a$, so its height is $3a$, and splitting it at $P$ into three triangles on equal bases shows that the distances from $P$ to its sides add up to $3a$. So $[PAB] + [PCD] + [PEF] = \frac{3}{2}sa = \frac{1}{2}H$. Subtracting, $[PAB] - [PBC] + [PCD] = \frac{1}{6}H$, so $H = 6(7 - 10 + 15) = 72$.

solution_figures.alt: Regular hexagon ABCDEF with a point P inside it, joined to all six vertices. Triangles PAB, PBC and PCD carry their areas 7, 10 and 15. The triangles PAB, PCD and PEF on alternate sides are shaded. The sides AB, CD and EF are extended to form a large equilateral triangle around the hexagon; the distances from P to its three sides add up to its height, so the shaded triangles make half of the hexagon. The opposite sides BC and EF are parallel, so triangles PBC and PEF make a third of it, and the hexagon has area 72.
